title: Wandering Merchant
body: A cloaked figure blocks your path, pack heavy with wares. They eye your party appraisingly. 'Rare goods for rare folk,' they say. 'What'll it be?'

choices.label: Browse their wares (spend 20 gold)
choices.resultText: You find a charm of warding among their stock.

choices.label: Ask for information instead
choices.resultText: The merchant points out a nearby landmark. 'Watch yourself out there.'

choices.label: Send them on their way
choices.resultText: They shrug and disappear down the path.

title: Abandoned Campsite
body: You find the remnants of a campsite: ashes still warm, bedrolls scattered. Whoever was here left in a hurry. A pack lies open near the fire pit.

choices.label: Search the pack carefully
choices.resultText: You find coin and dried rations.

choices.label: Rest here briefly
choices.resultText: The embers warm your hands. You take a moment to recover.

choices.label: Move on. This doesn't feel right
choices.resultText: Smart. You hear distant movement minutes later.

title: Fork in the Road
body: The path splits. A weathered signpost points two directions: one toward sounds of distant conflict, one into deeper wilderness. A third path looks recently cleared.

choices.label: Toward the conflict. Danger means opportunity
choices.resultText: You find the aftermath of a skirmish. Among the fallen, scattered coin.

choices.label: Into the wilderness
choices.resultText: The deep path is hard going, but you find an untouched cache.

choices.label: The cleared path
choices.resultText: It leads to a small sheltered hollow. A good place to rest.

title: Lost Traveler
body: A figure stumbles toward you, half-delirious from exposure. They clutch a sealed letter and beg you to deliver it. They seem too weak to make it themselves.

choices.label: Take the letter and the time to help them
choices.resultText: You guide them to safer ground. They press a small token of thanks into your hand.

choices.label: Take only the letter. They'll have to fend for themselves
choices.resultText: They watch you go without a word. The letter is heavier than it looked.

choices.label: Refuse and continue on
choices.resultText: They stagger off into the wilderness. You don't look back.

title: The Addressee
body: A waystone shrine marks the crossroads, its niche stacked with wax-stubs and older offerings. A robed keeper tends a low flame and watches you approach. This is the place named on the sealed letter's face, if you still carry it.

choices.label: Deliver the sealed letter
choices.resultText: The keeper breaks the seal, reads, and goes very still. 'You have no idea what you've carried.' They press coin on you and teach you a working held here for exactly this moment.

choices.label: Read the sigils warding the shrine
choices.resultText: The wards resolve under a trained eye, a scholar's shortcut. You note a cache the keeper never mentions.

choices.label: Buy a blessing from the keeper (40 gold)
choices.resultText: The keeper anoints your brow with warm ash. The road's aches recede.

choices.label: Leave an offering and move on
choices.resultText: You set a coin in the niche and go. The flame gutters once, as if in thanks.

title: A Familiar Face
body: A courier slows on the road, squinting at your party as if placing a memory. 'You're the ones who carried word to the shrine,' she says. Or maybe she's mistaken. She waits to see how you answer.

choices.label: Ask what the letter contained
choices.resultText: She lowers her voice. 'A name. An old debt, finally answered.' She leaves you a purse for your part in it.

choices.label: Accept her thanks and move on
choices.resultText: She clasps your arm. 'Kindness travels farther than you'd think.' The road feels shorter after.

choices.label: You must have us confused with someone else
choices.resultText: She shrugs, unconvinced, and rides on.

title: The Weaponsmith's Cache
body: A collapsed forge-shrine, its bellows long cold. Wrapped in oilcloth beneath the anvil lies a blade that never took the rust. Someone meant it to be found.

choices.label: Take the blade
choices.resultText: The grip fits your hand as if measured for it. It goes into the armory.

choices.label: Leave it for the next traveller
choices.resultText: Some gifts are meant to be passed along.

title: A Debt Repaid
body: A broad-shouldered figure steps from the treeline, hands open. Word of your deeds in these lands reached them before you did. 'You do right by strangers,' they say. 'Let me do right by you. I'll walk your road a while.'

choices.label: Welcome them to the guild
choices.resultText: They fall into step beside you, already at home.

choices.label: Thank them, but travel alone
choices.resultText: They nod, unoffended, and melt back into the green.

title: The Charter's Envoy
body: A rider in Free Charter colours reins in beside you, ledger open. 'The Charter remembers those who lend a hand on the frontier. Care to be remembered well?'

choices.label: Pledge aid to the Free Charter
choices.resultText: The envoy inks your name into the ledger with a flourish. Doors will open easier now.

choices.label: Keep your independence
choices.resultText: 'Suit yourself.' The rider tips a hat and moves on.

title: The Vault Inscription
body: A sealed vault door, its lock long fused, but the lintel above is dense with a script older than any kingdom. It tells of a concord that drowned itself rather than yield what it guarded.

choices.label: Copy the inscription in full
choices.resultText: Hours of careful transcription. The truth of the Sunken Concord is yours to keep.

choices.label: Note its location and move on
choices.resultText: Some readings are best done with more time than an expedition allows.

title: A Wayside Find
body: The path bends around {site}. {detail} {complication}

choices.label: Investigate closely
choices.resultText: You pick the place apart with care. It yields a little coin and a lot of unease.

choices.label: Mark it and move on
choices.resultText: You note the spot for later and keep your distance.

title: The Storm on the Horizon
body: Past the last ridge the sky is wrong: a wall of iron cloud that never moves, lightning frozen inside it mid-strike. The drowned archive named this place. If the rumour holds, the Primal Shard is in there.

choices.label: Chart a course into the tempest
choices.resultText: You map the eye of the storm and the paths that might survive it. The way is known now. The rest is nerve.

choices.label: Turn back. The storm is death unprepared
choices.resultText: Some doors you knock on twice.

title: The Warden of Elements
body: At the storm's threshold something waits: not a beast but a will, six elements braided into one guardian. It regards your party the way a furnace regards a moth. It will not simply let you pass.

choices.label: Speak to the storm in its own tongue
choices.resultText: Elemental cant answers elemental will. The warden yields to a kindred voice, and the way opens without blood.

choices.label: Face the Warden of Elements in battle
choices.resultText: No words will move it. Steel and spell, then.

choices.label: Withdraw and gather your strength
choices.resultText: The warden does not pursue. It has waited centuries; it can wait for you.

title: The Heart of the Storm
body: In the eye, everything is still. The Primal Shard hangs in the silence: raw creation, fire that does not burn, lightning frozen mid-strike. One of the six pieces of the Sixfold Seal. It is yours to take, and to answer for.

choices.label: Take the Primal Shard
choices.resultText: The Shard settles into your keeping, colder and heavier than anything its size should be. One fragment of the failing Seal, recovered. Five remain.

choices.label: Leave it. The world is not ready
choices.resultText: You close the way behind you. The Shard waits in the stillness, patient as the storm.

title: The Old Scout's Cairn
body: A stone cairn with a weathered tin box wedged in its base. Inside: trail notes in a dead scout's shorthand, half the marks worn away. Someone who knew the land wrote these.

choices.label: [Wayfarer's Map] Cross-reference the shorthand against your map
choices.resultText: The old marks and your map disagree in exactly the ways that matter. Three sites resolve out of the fog of guesswork.

choices.label: Puzzle out what you can
choices.resultText: Most of it is lost, but one mark is unmistakable.

choices.label: Leave the dead their secrets
choices.resultText: You stack a stone on the cairn and move on.

title: The Captured Courier
body: A courier sits trussed beside a cold campfire, abandoned by whoever caught them. Their satchel is gone but their memory isn't. 'Cut me loose and I'll tell you what roads I've run.'

choices.label: [Wren Holloway] Let Wren talk shop with a fellow traveler
choices.resultText: Wren trades road-gossip like currency. The courier's whole route spills out, landmark by landmark.

choices.label: Pay for the route (25 gold)
choices.resultText: Coin loosens a careful tongue. Two waypoints, precisely described.

choices.label: Cut them loose and ask nothing
choices.resultText: They vanish down the road. Word of the kindness travels ahead of you.

title: Signal Mirrors on the Ridge
body: Sun-flash from a ridgeline: an abandoned signal station, its bronze mirrors still true. From up here the land lays itself open, if you can work the old sight-lines.

choices.label: Work the mirrors through the morning (2 steps)
choices.resultText: Flash by flash, the country answers. You mark what moves and what doesn't.

choices.label: Pry a mirror loose to sell
choices.resultText: The bronze alone is worth the climb.

title: The Frozen Archive
body: A cold that shouldn't be here. Beneath a shelf of black ice, a reading-room stands unrotted. A scholar of your own discipline died mid-study, their working still open on the lectern.

choices.label: Thaw the pages and study the working
choices.resultText: The ice gives up its secret. You copy the technique before the cold takes it back.

choices.label: Take what gold survived and go
choices.resultText: You pocket a frostbitten purse and leave the dead to their reading.

title: The Watching Sigils
body: Sigils that seem to watch back. A collapsed athenaeum of your school still hums. One folio survived the fall, its diagrams answering questions you hadn't yet asked.

choices.label: Decipher the surviving folio
choices.resultText: The diagrams resolve into a method you did not know your discipline held.

choices.label: Leave the sigils to their vigil
choices.resultText: Some doors are best left closed. You step back into the light.

title: The Cinderleaf Folio
body: Ash falling from a clear sky. In the lee of a scorched shrine, a folio bound in your school's marks lies open. The fire read it before you did, but the last legible page is the one that matters.

choices.label: Salvage the last legible page
choices.resultText: You lift the page whole. The technique on it is yours now.

choices.label: Let the ash finish its work
choices.resultText: You leave the folio to the fire and move on.

title: The Crossing
body: The route ahead pinches down to a single line: {site}. {weather} {detail} You can take it at pace or take it carefully, and the third option involves walking back the way you came.

choices.label: Cross at speed
choices.resultText: You are over before the ground can form an opinion. Something in the packs is soaked and one ankle will complain about it for a day.

choices.label: Cross carefully, one at a time
choices.resultText: Roped, slow, and entirely unglamorous. Everyone reaches the far side with everything they started with.

choices.label: Walk the bank for a better line
choices.resultText: The better line does not exist. The hour spent looking for it does put something worth knowing on your map.

title: Somebody Else's Camp
body: {site}, and laid out around it the bones of a camp: stones shifted, ground trodden flat, a latrine dug at a respectful distance by people who knew what they were doing. {detail} {complication}

choices.label: Strip it properly
choices.resultText: An hour on your knees in someone else's leavings turns up a little coin and a great deal you would rather not have learned about them.

choices.label: Use it. It is a good site
choices.resultText: Whoever chose this ground chose well. You sleep better than you have any right to.

choices.label: Leave it exactly as you found it
choices.resultText: You touch nothing. Out here that is a currency, and it occasionally pays.

title: The Unburied
body: At {site} you find {figure}. {detail} Nobody came for them, and this far out nobody was ever going to.

choices.label: Bury them properly
choices.resultText: It costs you most of a morning and the use of two shovels. Their effects come to a handful of coin and a name, which you write down.

choices.label: Take what they no longer need
choices.resultText: They do not object. Nobody does. You are careful not to look at the face while you work.

choices.label: Mark the position and move on
choices.resultText: You set a stone upright so the next party sees it coming, and you keep walking.

title: A Shrine of Uncertain Provenance
body: {site}. Someone made a shrine of it. Not recently, and not to anything you can put a name to. {detail} {complication}

choices.label: Leave an offering
choices.resultText: You give up something you will miss. The road afterwards is easier than it has any business being, and you decline to examine why.

choices.label: Read the marks for a maker
choices.resultText: The hand is trained, the school is nobody's you were taught, and the sightlines the shrine was built along point somewhere specific.

choices.label: Take the offerings
choices.resultText: Coin, mostly, and older than it should be. Somebody put it here for a reason and now you are carrying the reason.

title: The Signal
body: {weather} Through it, from the direction of {site}, a signal comes: three flashes, a pause, three more. {complication} It is a recognition code, cleanly sent. It is not one of yours.

choices.label: Answer it
choices.resultText: You send back something plausible. What comes down the slope is not friendly, but it is negotiable, and it leaves you better off than it found you.

choices.label: Move to see who answers
choices.resultText: You spend the afternoon on your belly watching an exchange you were never meant to see. It is worth the afternoon.

choices.label: Break line of sight and go wide
choices.resultText: You put a ridge between yourself and the conversation. The detour costs you, and costs you nothing you will regret.

title: Terms on the Road
body: Where the ground opens out beside {site}, {figure} is waiting. They have goods, or say they do, and they name a price before you have said what you want. {detail}

choices.label: Buy what they are offering
choices.resultText: You are overcharged by a professional. What you get for it is real, which is more than most transactions out here manage.

choices.label: Sell them what you can spare
choices.resultText: They pay under value and both of you know it. Weight off your backs is worth something too.

choices.label: Decline and keep walking
choices.resultText: They call an improved price after you, twice, then stop. The second price was the honest one.

title: The Warning
body: Someone went to genuine trouble here: {site}, and on it a warning (cut, daubed or piled up) in a hand that plainly meant it. {detail} {complication}

choices.label: Heed it and route around
choices.resultText: The long way is longer. Nothing happens on it, which is the entire point of the long way.

choices.label: Press straight on
choices.resultText: The warning was accurate. It was also, in the end, survivable, and you make up the ground you would have lost going round.

choices.label: Work out who left it, and when
choices.resultText: The weathering says two seasons; the hand says a professional; the direction it faces says the danger is not where you assumed.

title: A Wound in the Ground
body: {site}. Except no weather opened this. Something took a piece out of the world here and the edges have never closed over. {weather} {complication}

choices.label: Go down into it
choices.resultText: The descent is worse than it looks and the bottom is worse than the descent. You come up with your hands full and your nerves shortened.

choices.label: Sound it from the lip
choices.resultText: Rope, weight, and patience. You learn how deep it goes and, from the echo, roughly what else is down there.

choices.label: Give it the width it deserves
choices.resultText: You walk the long arc around it. Nobody in the party suggests otherwise.

title: The Watcher
body: {figure}, at distance, on ground that gives them the better view of you. {detail} They have made no attempt at concealment, which means either they want to be seen or the question of being seen does not concern them.

choices.label: Walk up openly
choices.resultText: You go slow with your hands where they can be seen. The conversation is short, mostly one-sided, and ends with them handing you something.

choices.label: Circle and come at them from cover
choices.resultText: By the time you reach the spot they have gone, leaving a cold seat, a clear firing line, and a view of the country you had not thought to take.

choices.label: Let them watch, and go
choices.resultText: You keep formation, keep pace, and do not look up again. Whatever they wanted, they did not want it enough.

title: The Founder's Fork
body: A collapsed bell-foundry, and in the rubble of what was the tuning room a rack of forks in graded sizes, all but one snapped or corroded past use. The survivor is heavy, dull with age, and stamped with a mark you have seen over the Academy gate. Struck against the heel of your hand it gives a note that goes on considerably longer than it ought to.

choices.label: Take the fork
choices.resultText: It goes into your pack wrapped in cloth, and it hums faintly against your back for the rest of the day whenever the party crosses hard ground. Somewhere a bell has been waiting for this pitch for a very long time.

choices.label: Sound it properly first
choices.resultText: You strike it clean against stone and hold it up, and the note fills the foundry and keeps filling it. Two of your party sit down. When it finally fades you wrap the fork without discussion and carry it out.

choices.label: Strip the rack for scrap metal
choices.resultText: Good bronze, badly stored. You take the broken ones for weight and leave the sound one where it is, because taking it felt disproportionate and you decline to examine why.

title: An Order Never Delivered
body: A carter's depot on a road that used to run to the Academy, and the standing orders are still on the hook by the door: the ones that were loaded, the ones that were paid for, and at the bottom of the spike one that was neither. Flour, salt, three barrels of wine, for delivery on the morning of the commencement. The carter it was assigned to never came back for the slip.

choices.label: Buy the order out and take the slip
choices.resultText: The depot honours a paid order at any age, which is either admirable bookkeeping or a policy nobody has ever had to test. Flour, salt, and three barrels of wine, and the slip itself, which matters more.

choices.label: Take the slip and argue about the goods later
choices.resultText: You lift it off the spike while the clerk is turned around. It is a piece of paper recording a debt owed to a kitchen that has not served a meal in living memory, and you want it very badly.

choices.label: Read the whole spike
choices.resultText: Every undelivered order from that season, in date order. The last one is the commencement supply. The three above it are for the same address and were cancelled by the sender the previous week.

title: Heartleaf and Stillwater
body: The stand grows where the ground stays wet all year: heartleaf in the shade of the bank, stillwater moss under the surface in the slow part of the pool. Both are ordinary. Both are also the two reagents that a standing mending-weave burns through fastest, and somebody who knew that planted this stand deliberately, in rows, a very long time ago.

choices.label: Harvest carefully and leave the stand viable
choices.resultText: You cut what you need and no more, and re-lay the moss so the pool will carry it. It is patient work and the reagents come out at full strength, which the hurried version does not manage.

choices.label: Strip it
choices.resultText: You take all of it. The reagents are good and there are a great many of them, and the stand will not be here next season for anyone else who needs it.

choices.label: Find out who planted it
choices.resultText: The rows are on a spacing taught at exactly one institution, and the institution stopped teaching it before the Collapse. Whoever put this here expected to come back and harvest it for years.

title: The Abandoned Station
body: An observation post on high ground, abandoned in a hurry: the lens taken, the furniture left, and the night-ledgers still in the rack in date order. The last volume runs to within a week of the Sundering and then stops in the middle of an entry, mid-column, with the arithmetic unfinished and the pen still in the gutter of the page.

choices.label: Take the final volumes
choices.resultText: Three books covering the season either side of the Sundering, in the observer's own hand, with their working shown. It is the raw material for a counter-reading and it has been sitting on a shelf on a hill.

choices.label: Take the whole rack
choices.resultText: Eleven years of nightly observations. Most of it is unremarkable and all of it is continuous, and continuity is the thing that makes the last week mean anything.

choices.label: Read the unfinished entry and leave
choices.resultText: The arithmetic breaks off partway through a correction. The correction is large. Whatever the observer had just realised, they did not stay to finish writing it down.

title: The Foundational Text
body: A vault library, largely intact, and on the shelf the standard warding primer every apprentice of a certain generation was set to copy out by hand. This copy has been worked to death: annotated, disagreed with, argued into the margins in a small, fast, furious hand that treats the author as an opponent rather than a teacher. The annotator worked out how to break every ward in the book.

choices.label: Take the annotated copy
choices.resultText: The primer is worth little and the marginalia is worth a great deal. You now hold both halves of the argument: how the wards are built, and precisely how one person proved they could be taken apart.

choices.label: Take a clean copy from the shelf instead
choices.resultText: There are four unmarked copies beside it. You take one, and then you go back and take the annotated one as well, because leaving it here was never actually an option.

choices.label: Read the marginalia where it stands
choices.resultText: You get through perhaps a third. The hand is confident, the reasoning is correct, and the tone by the final chapters has stopped being academic entirely.
